are the two points that form the heart-essence of the Primal Vow Dharma-gate] This is what Master Hōnen himself said. Hōnen said:
The heart-essence of the
Pure Land school
lies in this: whoever it may be, anyone who recites the Buddha’s name attains rebirth.
Even a wicked person without peer
(unmatchable)
in the world
, if he recites Namo Amitābha Buddha,
will attain rebirth even with a single thought
This not only fails to grasp the heart-essence of Master Shandao, but deliberately
falsified
the Pure Land thought of Master Shandao, the manifestation of Amitābha, in order to establish the Primal Vow Dharma-gate
. For eight hundred years, who knows how many reciters it has misled in their wisdom-life!
Q: Master Daochuo said:

“If any sentient being, even if he commits evil throughout his life, at the moment of death continues ten recitations, calling upon my name, and is not reborn, then may I not attain perfect enlightenment.”

Since it says “even if one commits evil throughout one’s life,” as long as “at the moment of death the ten recitations continue,” one is certain to attain rebirth, so does that mean a reciter need not abandon evil and practice good? Is this so?
A:
“Even if one commits evil throughout one’s life, as long as at the moment of death the ten recitations continue, one is certain to attain rebirth”

indicates that right mindfulness at the moment of death, the continuation of the ten recitations, is of the utmost importance. That is to say, the continuity of the ten recitations at death is the sole requirement for rebirth; as long as the ten recitations continue at the moment of death, one can induce Amitābha Buddha to come and guide one across.

But to reach this requirement, one must in daily life accomplish the habit of continuing the ten recitations until it becomes second nature, and abandoning evil and practicing good are extremely important auxiliary conditions. Therefore Master Shandao taught:
“May all people reflect well within themselves; whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down,
one must exert one’s mind and restrain oneself,

abandoning not a single moment day or night. When the previous thought reaches life’s end, the next thought is rebirth. Forever enjoying the unconditioned joy of the Dharma, and on up to Buddhahood, how delightful that would be!”
The
“exert one’s mind and restrain oneself”

of which he spoke means to spur oneself on and to discipline oneself. A person who indulges himself and commits evil cannot achieve “exerting the mind and restraining oneself,” and is moreover out of accord with single-minded recitation free of confused thoughts.
On this, the Repentance Master Ciyun (Zunshi) taught:

“Thus, when one fixes one’s mind on the Buddha, spontaneously and constantly it of itself blocks all evil thoughts. If one is about to do evil, because one recollects the Buddha, the evil cannot come to be.”
The Two Gates of Resolving Doubts and Making the Vow of Rebirth in the Pure Land

Therefore, a person who does not exert his mind and restrain himself finds it hard to accomplish the habit of continuing the ten recitations until it becomes second nature, so the continuity of the ten recitations at death is not assured. Conversely, if one truly accomplishes the habit of continuing the ten recitations until it becomes second nature, one will not go on committing evil, because
“if one is about to do evil, because one recollects the Buddha, the evil cannot come to be”

There are also extremely rare exceptions in which one commits evil throughout one’s life and yet accomplishes “at the moment of death, the continuation of the ten recitations.” Such a case is that of a cultivator who, in a former life, already possessed considerable attainment, but because he had not completely cut off the delusions of view and thought, transmigrated into this life. In this life he again strayed onto a wrong path and committed evil throughout his life. At the moment of death, awakened by the instruction of a good friend, he repented with all his heart and accomplished the continuation of the ten recitations and was reborn. Consider: if it were not based upon the bodhi-mind and the profound attainment of a former life, how, amid the pressing together of all the miseries at the moment of death, could he suddenly give rise to faith and vows and abruptly accomplish the continuation of the ten recitations?

Therefore one must never imitate this, for among ten thousand people reborn in the Pure Land, hardly one is such a case. Consider: if one normally indulges one’s conduct and lets the mind do evil, and when adverse or favorable conditions arise the mind follows them away, then amid the pressing together of all the miseries at the moment of death, how could one accomplish the continuation of the ten recitations? On this principle, since ancient times the great masters and venerable ancestors have given many, many teachings and discussions.
